title: ldn Sysmodule ROP Gadget Catalog — ARM64

notes.aslr: 17-bit entropy, 2MB-aligned. All addresses below are base-relative (subtract 0x7100000000 to get file offset). At runtime, add the actual module base.
notes.mitigations: NX enabled (need ROP), no PAC, no stack canaries on Erista
notes.search_coverage: Full binary (961288 bytes) searched for each pattern

stack_pivot_epilogues.description: ldp x29, x30, [sp], #N; ret — restore frame pointer + return address from stack, advance SP, return. These are the backbone of any ROP chain.

register_control_epilogues.description: Multi-register ldp sequences before the stack pivot + ret. These load callee-saved registers from the stack, giving full register control for subsequent gadgets.

x19_x23_control_0x40.side_effect: w0 = w20 (sets return value from stack-controlled x20)
x19_x23_control_0x40.note: BEST x0-setter: sets w0=w20 before return, x20 loaded from sp+0x30

x19_x28_control_0x60_full.note: MASTER GADGET: controls ALL callee-saved registers x19-x28 from stack

x23_x28_control_0x60.note: In the vulnerable consumer function FUN_7100037dc0 — directly reachable from overflow

x19_x28_control_with_sp_adjust.note: Preceded by add sp, sp, #N — additional SP adjustment before register restore

indirect_call_gadgets.description: blr xN — branch to register with link. Used to call arbitrary functions after register setup.

best_examples.note: Preceded by cbz x8 — skips call if x8=0 (safe). After call: branch back, then ldp x20,x19; ldp x29,x30; ret

blr_x8.note: x8 is the standard indirect call register in ARM64 ABI. Control via register_control_epilogues (x8 not callee-saved — need a load gadget or use as part of a function's prologue)

svc_stubs.description: Horizon OS system call stubs. These are the actual SVC instruction wrappers in the SDK. Addresses are for direct calls from ROP.

svcWaitSynchronization.wrapper: SVC #0x18; ldr x2,[sp]; str w1,[x2]; add sp,sp,#0x10; ret
svcWaitSynchronization.note: Returns result via stack pointer; multi-instruction wrapper

svcConnectToNamedPort.note: Multi-instruction wrapper with stack save; CRITICAL for IPC

svcSendSyncRequest.note: CRITICAL: core IPC mechanism for all service calls

svcOutputDebugString.note: Useful for debugging exploit — write strings to kernel log

svcGetInfo.note: Returns system info; can leak ASLR base via InfoType

mov_x0_gadgets.description: Gadgets that set x0 (first argument / return value) from a stack-controlled register. No direct mov-ret pairs found; all go through epilogue register restores.

mov_x0_x19.note: Very common. Chain: use register_control to set x19, then jump to this, x0 gets x19's value. Always followed by more instructions before ret.

mov_x0_x20.note: Common pattern in virtual dispatch sequences

mov_w0_w20_with_epilogue.instruction_sequence: mov w0, w20; ldp x20,x19,[sp,#0x30]; ldp x22,x21,[sp,#0x20]; ldr x23,[sp,#0x10]; ldp x29,x30,[sp],#0x40; ret
mov_w0_w20_with_epilogue.note: BEST: sets w0 from w20 AND restores x19-x23, all from stack. Single gadget for x0 control + chain continuation.

function_targets.description: Key functions to call from ROP chain for exploitation

memcpy.note: thunk_FUN_71000a8540 — the same memcpy used by the vulnerable function
memcpy.usage: memcpy(dst, src, len) — for writing controlled data to arbitrary addresses

vulnerable_function.name: FUN_710003b470
vulnerable_function.note: The vulnerable frame extractor itself — could be re-triggered

consumer_loop.note: Main frame processing — where overflow occurs during normal execution

rop_chain_strategy.overview: The heap overflow at FUN_710003b470 corrupts adjacent heap data. The chain requires: (1) hijack control flow via corrupted vtable/function pointer, (2) pivot stack to controlled data, (3) execute ROP chain to call svcSendSyncRequest for IPC, escalating to code execution.

step_1_hijack.description: Corrupt a vtable pointer or function pointer on the heap adjacent to the overflowed output struct (0x798 bytes each in an array)
targets: Adjacent output struct's vtable pointer (at struct+0x00)

step_2_stack_pivot.description: Need to pivot SP to attacker-controlled data. Options:
step_2_stack_pivot.option_a: If we control a vtable, point it at a function that does `add sp, xN, #imm` or `mov sp, xN` where xN is controlled
step_2_stack_pivot.option_b: Corrupt return address on actual stack via adjacent stack frame corruption
step_2_stack_pivot.option_c: Use `ldp x29, x30, [sp], #N; ret` chain starting from corrupted heap metadata that affects stack operations

step_3_register_setup.description: Use master gadget at 0x7100011f20 to control x19-x28, then chain to mov-x0 gadget
gadget_chain: 0x710000af78: mov w0, w20 + restore + ret (sets first argument)
Target function call or SVC wrapper

step_4_svc_call.description: Call svcSendSyncRequest (0x7100023d94) or svcConnectToNamedPort (0x7100023d7c) for IPC to other services
escalation_path: Connect to sm: (service manager) via svcConnectToNamedPort
Use IPC to load custom NRO/NSO or modify memory mappings

aslr_considerations.brute_force: ~65K average attempts via repeated frame injection
aslr_considerations.info_leak_alternative: svcGetInfo (0x7100023ddc) can return module base if called with right InfoType — but requires initial code execution first
aslr_considerations.partial_overwrite: If heap layout allows, partial pointer overwrite (1-2 bytes) may bypass ASLR for nearby targets

summary.register_control: Full x19-x28 control from stack (master gadget at 0x7100011f20)
summary.x0_setter: mov w0, w20 at 0x710000af78 (with full epilogue)
summary.svc_stubs: 15+ HOS SVCs mapped (svcSendSyncRequest, svcConnectToNamedPort, svcGetInfo, etc.)
summary.assessment: SUFFICIENT gadgets for full ROP chain. The binary provides all primitives needed: register control, indirect calls, syscall stubs, and stack frame management. The main challenge is the initial control flow hijack from heap overflow and ASLR bypass.
